clue.text: No point in lots of boobs — leads to objections

indicators.note: 'No point' tells us a compass point is to be dropped from the word before it

parts.note: boobs are breasts, and lots of them are busts
S, south, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A complaint that a show full of nudity is pointless prompts protests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes one S (south, a point of the compass) from BUSTS, leaving the letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A 'but' is a spoken reservation or protest, as in 'no ifs or buts'.

clue.text: Hopeless type is mean to include one unfinished drawing

indicators.note: the first word is made to include, or hold, what follows

parts.note: base means low or mean in character

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: a sketch is a quick drawing
A is one, as in 'a pound'

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that a mean critic only ever produced half a sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like the adjective for a stingy person but is the low sense; 'unfinished' trims the drawing to SKETC, and 'to include' sets that plus A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A basket case is informal for a person or thing too incapable or broken to function.

clue.text: G-string air given by person with lisp

indicators.note: a lisping speaker turns the S sound into a TH sound, so the word is altered that way

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: Someone with a lisp sings about skimpy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: A lisp turns the S of SONG into TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a skimpy garment of the G-string kind.

clue.text: Lord's must have one and won't

definitions.text: Lord's must have one and won't

parts.words: Lord's must have one and won't
parts.note: Lord's, the London cricket ground, is always written with a punctuation mark, and so is the contraction won't; the surface reads as a stubborn lord refusing

explanation.surface: A nobleman insists on having something but then refuses.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a peer's whims; it is really about the punctuation mark in the written words Lord's and won't. LORD'S is a famous London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Both written forms need the raised comma punctuation mark, one for possession, one for a contraction.

clue.text: Sprain discovered in favourite male deer

indicators.note: the first item is found inside the second word

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
rick is a dialect or dated word for a sprain or twist

explanation.surface: A treasured stag is found to have twisted a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sprain' reads as a verb in the surface, but rick is an old word for a sprain; 'discovered in' shows it sitting inside the favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A pricket is a male fallow deer in its second year, with straight unbranched horns.

clue.text: Editor's amazing performance enhancer

indicators.note: amazing suggests something bewildered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor raves about a dramatic drug scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazing' looks like praise but asks for EDITORS (including the S of the possessive) to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic steroids are drugs athletes take illegally to boost strength and results.

clue.text: Move plant in boozer upwards

indicators.note: in a down clue, upwards means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A gardener shifts a pot plant inside a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'boozer' is the drinker, not the pub; TOPER read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To repot is to transfer a plant into a new container.

clue.text: Stern ad starts to impact on roads

parts.note: a poster is an advertisement

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: A harsh advertising campaign hits motorists on the roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' is not the adjective here but the rear end, as of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the back of a ship, and the posterior is the rear or backside.

clue.text: Cupid's showing love's not unknown

indicators.note: not says the following letter is left out of the word

parts.note: love is a score of nothing in tennis, so loves are zeros
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: Cupid shows that love isn't a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove Z (an algebraic unknown) from ZEROS (loves, nil scores in tennis).
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of desire, matching the Roman Cupid.

clue.text: Edison's partner lied, perhaps, in final appearance

parts.note: Joseph Swan partnered Thomas Edison in the Ediswan lamp company
a lied is a German art song, an example of a song

explanation.surface: An inventor's associate told a fib, maybe, in his last show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lied' looks like 'told a lie' but is the German word for a song; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan song is a farewell performance, from the legend that swans sing before dying.

clue.text: Animated miners' leader not colourful

definitions.meaning: in the Disney cartoon, the seven dwarfs who work in a mine follow a fairytale princess

explanation.walkthrough: 'Animated' suggests a lively union boss; it means a cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairytale princess leads the dwarf miners in Disney's cartoon; snow-white also means spotlessly pale.

clue.text: Sauce is nuisance on ring

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A cheeky person phones someone who is a pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' could mean cheek, but here it is the Italian basil sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian basil, garlic and pine-nut sauce.

clue.text: Urge one gets before toast

definitions.meaning: to egg someone on is to urge them
in the phrase about breakfast food, these words come before 'toast', with an oval food that is laid upon bread

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: these words precede 'toast' in a familiar breakfast phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur on someone is to encourage them; a breakfast order with a boiled item placed on bread begins with these words.

clue.text: Row with small group of people is more puzzling

parts.note: a knot is a small cluster of people
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A dispute within a small group gets ever more baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' is a line of seats, not an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotty means complicated, so the comparative means more complicated or baffling.

clue.text: Scrap that's universally welcome?

definitions.meaning: a scrap is a brawl or fight
open to everyone at no charge

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a bit of waste, but it is a brawl involving all comers.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorderly fight with everyone joining in; also something open to everyone at no cost.

clue.text: A cigar is champion in bed

indicators.note: in puts the second word inside the first

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
a hero is a champion

explanation.surface: A champion smokes a cigar in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A cigar' is the definition including its article; the champion sits 'in' the small bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar with both ends cut square.

clue.text: Former partner, one on speed let off

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a rate is a speed

explanation.surface: An ex caught speeding is let off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to clear or absolve someone of blame.

clue.text: Brief kip for tramp? That's right

parts.note: a doss is a rough sleep, the kind a vagrant gets
IE (id est) means 'that is'

explanation.surface: A short nap for a vagrant is quite proper, someone remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like 'short' but is the noun, a set of papers. 'That's' is 'that is', i.e. IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a collection of documents on a subject, like a lawyer's case papers.

clue.text: What printing strikers do in break

definitions.meaning: striking print workers halt production of the sheets

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition splits the word into two: striking printers halt the sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking print workers halt the press run; a stoppage is a halt or interruption.

clue.text: Soprano recorded hit

parts.note: logged means recorded

explanation.surface: A soprano's song was taped and became a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' looks like a chart success but is the verb, struck hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To slog is to strike hard, as a batsman does.

clue.text: Forget serious offence in visits

parts.note: to drop a subject is to forget it
a sin is a serious offence

explanation.surface: A guest who drops by is told to forgive a grave wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop in is to pay a casual call on someone.

clue.text: A whip is good source in reshuffle

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the rearranged word
a reshuffle rearranges, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A party whip is a good source of news during a cabinet reshuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip' suggests a party enforcer; here it is a lash. SOURCE rearranged gives SCOURE, with G placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a whip used for punishment.

clue.text: Such is a good weather forecast just after a few games

definitions.text: Such is a good weather forecast

indicators.note: after places the second word behind the first

parts.note: in tennis, a set is a group of games
fair means just

explanation.surface: The forecast looks good just after a few tennis games.
explanation.walkthrough: A set in tennis is a group of games, so 'a few games' is the tennis word; 'after' puts 'just' behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Set fair describes settled fine weather, as forecast on a barometer.

clue.text: Fish behind course with no end of trouble

parts.note: the seat is a person's behind

indicators.note: with no says the following letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a route is a course

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone fishes behind the course with no trouble at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks positional but is the bottom; ROUTE loses its E, the last letter of 'trouble'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea trout is a migratory brown trout that lives in the sea.

clue.text: Flipping nifty vehicles

indicators.note: flipping turns the word over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: smart means nifty or stylish

explanation.surface: Someone praises some flipping nifty cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British expletive, but signals a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Trams are street vehicles running on rails.

clue.text: Publicity for cats half obscured

parts.note: pro means for, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: half obscured means only the first two letters of the word are visible

parts.note: mog is British slang for a cat

explanation.surface: A cat food ad campaign is half hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: MOG is British slang for a cat; 'half obscured' hides the second half of MOGS. 'for' is the pro of 'pros and cons'.
explanation.definitionFit: A promo is a promotional piece of publicity.

clue.text: Hardy mostly seen in shades of green

definitions.note: the colour name covers a range of dull yellowish greens

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Oliver Hardy was the heavier half of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy

explanation.surface: Thomas Hardy's novels are mostly set in green countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' suggests the novelist; it is the comedian Oliver Hardy, losing his final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a dull yellowish-green colour.

clue.text: Strike in second leg

parts.note: a lap is a leg of a race

explanation.surface: A footballer is hit on the leg in a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leg' is a stage of a race, not a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To slap is to hit with an open hand.

clue.text: Animal turned back in a famous London thoroughfare

indicators.note: turned back means the whole phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: the Mall is the avenue leading to Buckingham Palace

explanation.surface: An animal loose on the Mall is turned back.
explanation.walkthrough: A MALL read backwards gives the animal. THE MALL is the ceremonial road to Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: A llama is a South American pack animal of the camel family.

clue.text: Hans involved with a girl — it's heaven!

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Hans is romantically involved with a girl and finds it heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' looks romantic but asks for HANS and A GIRL to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Shangri-La is an imaginary earthly paradise from James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon.

clue.text: Rustic class holding line with agreeable remark

indicators.note: holding means the first word contains the second

parts.note: the peasantry is the class of country labourers

explanation.surface: Country folk holding the line make a friendly comment.
explanation.walkthrough: L (line) goes inside PEASANTRY (rustic class).
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a polite, light remark made in conversation.

clue.text: Highland moor is fine for Welsh in spring

indicators.note: 'fine for Welsh' means one letter takes the place of the other in the word

parts.note: a well is a spring of water
F is short for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A Welsh moorland is fine when walked in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: In WELL (spring), F (fine) replaces W (Welsh).
explanation.definitionFit: A fell is a stretch of upland moor or hill, especially in northern England.
